Nicotine pouch withdrawal timeline: what to expect, hour by hour

This timeline is for people quitting nicotine pouches such as Zyn, Velo or On!, and snus. Times count from your last pouch. Everyone is different, so treat the times as typical, not exact.

Short answer. Withdrawal is usually worst in the first 2–3 days. It mostly fades within one to four weeks: Sweden's health service 1177 says one to three weeks, Norway's Directorate of Health says two to four. Single cravings can come back later, especially in old routines, and each one passes within minutes.

The timeline

  1. 20 minutes

    A craving lasts minutes, not hours

    The first cravings often come early. Each one usually passes within a few minutes, and 1177 puts a typical craving at just 20–30 seconds. Have a plan ready: a glass of water, a short walk or a call to a friend.

    Sources: Helsenorge, 1177.se

  2. 2 hours

    The nicotine in your blood is falling

    Nicotine has a half-life of about 2 hours, though it varies from person to person. A pouch releases nicotine slowly, so the level doesn't drop off a cliff, but it is already going down.

    Source: Benowitz et al., Handbook of Experimental Pharmacology, 2009

  3. 8 hours

    Your heart gets a break

    While a pouch is in, nicotine narrows blood vessels and raises your pulse and blood pressure. Nicotine pouches contain nicotine too, so they can have the same effect. Without nicotine, that extra load is gone.

    Source: Helsenorge: Snus – helseskader

  4. 24 hours

    Withdrawal signs are common now

    Restlessness, irritability, anxiety, low mood, poor sleep, trouble focusing and a bigger appetite are all normal withdrawal signs. They are unpleasant, and they pass.

    Source: 1177.se: Hjälp att sluta snusa

  5. 48 hours

    The hardest stretch

    In the Norwegian national guideline on quitting snus, withdrawal is worst in the first two to three days. If today feels rough, that is expected. It gets easier from here.

    Source: Helsedirektoratet: national guideline, Snus

  6. 72 hours

    Most of nicotine's breakdown product is gone

    Your body turns nicotine into cotinine, which has a half-life of about 16 hours. After three days, most of it has cleared. Small amounts can still show up in a test for a while, especially if you used a lot.

    Source: Benowitz et al., 2009

  7. 1 week

    Hungrier than usual

    Nicotine dampens hunger and speeds up metabolism, so feeling hungrier after quitting is common and normal. Keep water and a healthy snack nearby, and move a bit more if you can.

    Source: Helsenorge

  8. 2 weeks

    Your gums

    After quitting tobacco snus, irritated gums usually recover within a few weeks. Irritation from nicotine pouches can take months to heal. Gums that have pulled back don't grow back on their own. More in gums after quitting.

    Sources: University of Gothenburg, 2025, Helsenorge

  9. 1 month

    Withdrawal is mostly behind you

    Withdrawal symptoms usually fade within one to three weeks. A bigger appetite and the odd craving can stay longer, and that doesn't mean something went wrong.

    Source: 1177.se

  10. 3 months

    New routines settle in

    In studies of new health habits, routines took about two to five months to become automatic. Morning coffee without a pouch, a drive without a pouch: your new routines are well on the way. These studies were about building new habits, not quitting nicotine, so take this as a rough guide.

    Source: Singh et al., Healthcare, 2024 (systematic review)

  11. 6 months

    A quit that counts

    Studies of quitting snus and other smokeless tobacco count a quit as successful when it lasts six months or more. By that standard, yours counts.

    Source: Cochrane review: Interventions for smokeless tobacco use cessation, 2025

  12. 1 year

    The money adds up

    A year without buying pouches is a real sum. One $6 can every two days, for example, is about $1,100 a year. A common tip is to put that money toward something you really want.

    Source: Helsenorge

Questions people ask

Which day is the worst?

Usually day 2 or 3. The Norwegian guideline on quitting snus puts the peak in the first two to three days.

How long does nicotine pouch withdrawal last?

For most people, one to four weeks. Cravings tied to habits, such as coffee, driving or a night out, can turn up for longer, but they get weaker and rarer.

How long does a craving last?

From under a minute to a few minutes. Waiting it out with water, a walk or a message to a friend works better than fighting it in your head.

Will I gain weight?

A bigger appetite is a normal withdrawal sign and can last longer than the rest. Water, regular meals and a bit more movement help.

Can nicotine replacement help?

Yes, it can ease withdrawal. Helsenorge lists gum, patches, lozenges, mouth spray and pouches sold as medicines. Use the recommended dose: too weak a dose for too short a time makes a relapse more likely. Ask a pharmacist or doctor, and see cut down or quit cold turkey.

What this page leaves out, and why

Many quit timelines promise better lungs, a cleaner sense of smell or "carbon monoxide back to normal". Those findings are about smoking. Pouches and snus don't involve smoke, so we leave them out. We also don't claim that nicotine is "fully gone" by a certain hour: the timer starts when the last pouch went in, and people break nicotine down at different speeds.

Free help

US: 1-800-QUIT-NOW and the free EX Program. Sweden: Sluta röka-linjen, 020-84 00 00. Norway: the free Slutta app from Helsenorge. Denmark: Stoplinien, 80 31 31 31.
